description: Temporary change of use for the Unit 5, 189 Pasadena Close, from a storage into a Food retail business. Erection of fence around Unit 189.
decision_conditions: The proposed temporary change of use from an industrial warehouse unit to food retail (Use Class E) is unacceptable as it would result in the unjustified loss of industrial floorspace within a Strategic Industrial Location, where such uses are protected. The applicant has failed to demonstrate a lack of demand or provide robust evidence of active marketing in accordance with Policy DME1, and insufficient information has been submitted to show that the proposed use would be ancillary or compatible with the industrial function of the area. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy SEA1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 (2012), Policy DME1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), and Policy E5 of the London Plan (2021).

The proposed change of use from an industrial warehouse unit (Use Class B8) to a food retail use (Use Class E), together with the erection of perimeter fencing, is unacceptable as the application fails to provide sufficient, accurate and consistent information to enable a full assessment of its impact on the local highway network. In particular, the submitted plans are inconsistent and do not clearly identify the site, layout or access arrangements, and no justification or strategy has been provided for the loss of existing on-site parking or for servicing and delivery arrangements. The proposed use is likely to generate a higher level of customer and servicing trips, which in the absence of adequate on-site provision would result in overspill parking, obstruction of roads and harm to highway safety and the free flow of traffic. The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
